chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad narrated to me from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Kathir, from Harun ibn Kharija, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Indeed, they believe that whoever visits the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), it counts as his Hajj and Umrah.' He said: 'Whoever visits, by Allah, knowing his right, Allah will forgive him what preceded of his sin and what followed.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting Imam Husain's grave according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A’mal*, Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) clarifies that the promise of a visit to Imam Husayn’s shrine equating to a complete Hajj and Umrah is contingent upon *‘irfan* (gnostic recognition) of his specific right and status, rather than mere physical presence. This distinction underscores the Shia emphasis on the spiritual depth of *Ziyarat* as an act of affirming the Imamate, linking the pilgrim’s internal conviction directly to the absolution of all sins, past and future.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 5. It was narrated to me by al-Hussain b. Ahmad from his father from Muhammad b. Ahmad from Muhammad b. al-Hussain from al-Hassan b. Ali b. Fadhal from Muhammad b. al-Hussain b. Katheer from Harun b. Kharija who said:
“One who does Ziyarat of Imam Husain (a.s.) knowing his right, the Almighty Allah forgives all his past and future sins.”
